clue.text: Quietly grumble, rejecting drink twice

indicators.note: twice says the reversed drink appears two times in a row
rejecting means the drink is sent back, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a stock crossword drink

explanation.surface: Someone mutters complaints after turning down a second round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns RUM into MUR, and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutter discontent under your breath is a low, soft complaint.

clue.text: Pure in make-up, but not fully developed

indicators.note: make-up is composition, so the letters of the preceding words are made up afresh

explanation.surface: Something is pure in composition yet still immature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in make-up' rearranges the six letters of PURE IN; the 'in' is fodder, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit not yet ripe is immature, still short of full growth.

clue.text: Dandy that appears dishy, from Italy?

definitions.meaning: an eighteenth-century fop who affected Continental fashions was so called
a pasta that turns up as a dish, originating in Italy

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an affected Georgian fop and a tube-shaped Italian pasta.

clue.text: Contact bloke on eastern border of enclosure

parts.note: to ring someone is to contact them by phone
Sid is a typical man's name

explanation.surface: Someone gets in touch with a man at the east side of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The area beside a boxing or circus ring is the edge of that enclosed space.

clue.text: Servant, along with mother, took cover outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for took cover goes around the other pieces

parts.note: hid means took cover
and means along with
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A servant and her mother sheltered outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A female attendant or maid is a servant.

clue.text: Sort of gear a learner replaces on leaving Greek mountain

indicators.note: replaces says the new letters take the place of the departing ones
leaving names which letters quit the mountain's name

parts.note: Helicon is the Greek mountain sacred to the Muses
taken as written
taken as written
L is the learner-driver abbreviation

explanation.surface: A mechanic swaps a component after descending a mountain in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces' and 'on leaving': take ON out of HELICON and put A plus L in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Helical gears have spiral-cut teeth, so the word describes a type of gear.

clue.text: Arrange to meet girl to tour Lima — it should bear fruit

parts.note: to date someone is to arrange to meet them romantically

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the girl's name goes around the letter for Lima

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a date with a girl to visit Peru's capital, hoping it pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the Peruvian city but is the radio-alphabet word for L.
explanation.definitionFit: This palm tree produces dates, so it is expected to yield fruit.

clue.text: Party for some who may have gone downhill fast

definitions.text: Party for some who may have gone downhill fast

parts.words: Party for some who may have gone downhill fast
parts.note: gone downhill reads as declined, but means skied down slopes; the party is the evening socialising after a day on the piste

explanation.definitionFit: Evening socialising at a ski resort follows the day's skiing, which is what the French phrase means.

clue.text: Late Australian sheep-shearer's lookalike

parts.note: late means dead
in Australia a ringer is the fastest shearer in a shed

explanation.surface: A deceased shearer from Australia had a double.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is the exact image of another person is that person's double.

clue.text: Biscuit fellow turned over after funny remark

indicators.note: after places the reversed name behind the joke

parts.note: a crack is a wisecrack, a joke

indicators.note: turned over means the man's name is flipped and read backwards

parts.note: Len is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man flips over a cookie after making a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, crisp brittle biscuit goes by this old name.

clue.text: These bones are more rigid, so it's said

indicators.note: so it's said tells us the answer is how the word for more rigid sounds when spoken

parts.note: sterner means stricter, more rigid

explanation.surface: Some bones are described as stiffer than others.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the final -ER sounds like -A.
explanation.definitionFit: Breastbones are plural, the Latin plural of the anatomical name.

clue.text: Bliss, possibly, for one who scores runs

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur Bliss was an English Master of the Queen's Music, so an example of a writer of music
writes musical scores containing runs, rapid passages, not a cricketer making runs

explanation.definitionFit: A writer of music both is exemplified by Bliss and arranges notes into scores.

clue.text: Miss living in Barcelona?

parts.note: Miss is the title for an unmarried woman; in Spain she has her own Spanish title

explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish title for an unmarried young woman corresponds to Miss.

clue.text: Dupe Observer over this material?

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the observer above, before, the dupe

parts.note: a seer is one who sees, an observer
a sucker is someone easily duped

explanation.surface: A newspaper fools someone about a fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Observer looks like the newspaper but means a SEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton or linen fabric.

clue.text: Agitated former partner summoned to appear in court

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to be cited is to be summoned before a court

explanation.surface: Someone's ex is nervous about being called to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up or stirred up means being agitated.

clue.text: Two-timing double missing trip on ferry?

indicators.note: missing says the word double is taken away from the betrayal word

parts.note: double-crossing means betraying, two-timing

explanation.surface: A cheating lover misses a boat trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey across water by boat is a passage from shore to shore.

clue.text: Trio on river, including quiet farm-worker

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the river letter
including says the trio's word holds the call for silence inside it

parts.note: a trio is three
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Three people on a riverbank, including a silent one, work on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer who beats grain from the husks is a farmhand.

clue.text: A shepherd's work takes some beating — having change of heart?

indicators.note: change of heart says the middle letter of the beating word is swapped for another

parts.note: lamming is a thrashing, a beating

explanation.surface: A shepherd's work is hard to beat, unless one has a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes some beating' reads as praise but hides LAMMING; 'change of heart' turns its middle M into B.
explanation.definitionFit: Helping ewes deliver their young is the shepherd's spring task.

clue.text: Female collaborator seen round university at regular intervals

parts.note: Ann is a female name
an ally is a collaborator

explanation.surface: A woman working with someone is spotted around campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done each year happens at yearly, regular intervals.

clue.text: Resort of bishop with progressive views

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
right-on means holding fashionably liberal views

explanation.surface: A bishop with liberal opinions visits the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a well-known English seaside resort town.

clue.text: In South Carolina they designed 'sails, initially, for cutters

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina

indicators.note: designed implies something worked out anew, so the letters are rearranged
initially picks out the opening letter of sails

explanation.surface: In South Carolina people designed sails for small boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-bladed tools for mowing grass are cutting implements.

clue.text: Have regard for feelings of judge

definitions.meaning: to take someone's feelings into account
to judge is to deem or reckon

explanation.definitionFit: To deem something so is to judge it, and to think of others' feelings is to be thoughtful toward them.

clue.text: Appear to be upset, say, about the compiler

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the whole run of pieces upside down, reading bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
re means about, concerning
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A setter seems distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into view is to appear.

clue.text: Improper to appear in university, only just missing first

indicators.note: in places the word for appear inside the other letters
just missing first says only the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to seem is to appear

explanation.surface: It is unseemly to show up at university when only just failing the top grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just missing first' drops the O of ONLY, giving NLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is unbecoming is not proper.

clue.text: Errant type once given place on board?

definitions.meaning: a medieval mounted warrior errant wandered in search of adventure
a piece on the chessboard, also someone given a seat at a round table

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a wandering medieval warrior and a chess piece shaped like a horse.

clue.text: Short break for people of various classes

definitions.text: Short break for people of various classes

parts.words: Short break for people of various classes
parts.note: classes reads as social ranks, but means school forms; the short break comes in mid-term

explanation.definitionFit: A brief school holiday in the middle of a term gives pupils of every form a rest.

clue.text: Severe operatic prince interrupting wake finally ejected

indicators.note: interrupting puts the prince between letters of the waking word
finally ejected removes the last letter of the waking word

parts.note: to rouse is to wake
Prince Igor is Borodin's opera

explanation.surface: A harsh opera prince breaks in on a wake, finally being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wake' looks like a funeral vigil but is the verb; Prince Igor is the title role of Borodin's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and harsh in exactness means severe.

clue.text: After year on river, went off to place indicated

indicators.note: After places the remaining pieces behind the year letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: off says the word went is removed from the river's name

parts.note: the Derwent is a river in England

explanation.surface: After a year on a river, someone left for a spot pointed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went off' takes WENT from DERWENT, leaving DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Over there, the spot pointed to, is the old word's sense.
